◇ Note. The blasphemer’s execution. The chapter records the OT’s only narrative of capital punishment for blasphemy — and the procedure it institutes (the witnesses lay hands on the offender’s head before execution) becomes the standard Israelite procedure for capital cases. The hand-laying gesture is theologically charged: the witnesses transfer responsibility for the death from the community generally to themselves specifically. The same gesture appears in priestly ordination (Lev 8:14), in Joshua’s commissioning by Moses (Num 27:18), and in Christian sacramental ordination across the centuries — the gesture transmits authority and obligation simultaneously. The blasphemer’s execution also illustrates one of the OT’s most-discussed legal principles: the same law applies to native Israelite and resident alien (24:16, 22). The provision is one of the OT’s clearest articulations of equal application of capital law regardless of ethnic identity, an unusual position in ANE legal contexts where most law-codes had distinct procedures for the various social classes.

◇ Note. The valuation table. The chapter codifies a sliding-scale valuation system for persons dedicated to Yahweh: adult men 50 shekels, adult women 30, boys 20, girls 10, etc. (27:3–7). The differential valuation has generated significant ethical discussion — modern readers often experience it as discriminatory pricing of human worth. Rabbinic and modern critical scholarship offer multiple readings: the values may reflect typical economic productivity in ancient Israelite agricultural-pastoral economies (men producing more market value than women) without implying intrinsic worth distinctions; or they may encode patriarchal valuation that the chapter takes for granted; or they may function as a graduated pricing system to make vow-redemption affordable across different household economies. The chapter ends Leviticus with a note about how vows of persons are to be redeemed financially rather than literally enforced — the final word of the book is a procedural mercy, allowing rash dedications to be commuted to silver. The structural placement matters: Leviticus closes by limiting the binding force of religious enthusiasm.

◇ Note. The tithe principle. The chapter institutes the basic tithe — one-tenth of agricultural produce belonging to Yahweh — that becomes one of the OT’s most enduring cultic-economic obligations. The provision interlocks with several others: the priestly portion (Num 18:21–28), the triennial tithe for the poor (Deut 14:28–29), and Jacob’s pre-legal vow of tithing (Gen 28:22). By the Second Temple period, tithing had become one of the most-discussed legal-religious topics; Jesus’ critique that the Pharisees "tithe mint and dill and cumin and have neglected the weightier matters of the law" (Matt 23:23) reflects the technical elaboration the practice had received. Christian tradition has continued to treat tithing as theologically meaningful, though usually with debate over whether it remains literally binding. The verse is the textual root of one of the most economically and pastorally consequential OT institutions, with effects running into the modern church.

◇ Note. The verse and its interpretation. The verse — paired with the capital-penalty version at 20:13 — is one of the most contested texts in modern biblical interpretation. Several distinct interpretive traditions exist: traditional readings (rabbinic, patristic, and most Reformation-era and contemporary conservative Christian) take the verse as a categorical prohibition of male same-sex intercourse; some modern revisionist readings (so John Boswell, Robert Gagnon’s opponents in detail) argue the verse targets specific cultic-prostitution practices, exploitative or coercive acts, or pederasty rather than mutual consensual relationships; other modern readers (so Walter Wink) acknowledge the literal prohibition but treat it as part of the OT purity-code that the New Testament’s explicit suspension of the food-and-purity laws (Acts 10–11, 15) substantially reframes; and there is a long tradition of LGBTQ Jewish and Christian readers who have engaged the text from within their own communities of interpretation. The chapter’s placement of this prohibition among a list including incest (18:6–18), child sacrifice (18:21), bestiality (18:23), and adultery (18:20) frames the categorization the original editor intended. Few verses in the OT have generated more sustained scholarly, ecclesial, and personal debate, and the careful interpreter holds the literal sense of the verse together with the long range of interpretive engagement it has produced.

◇ Note. The high priest’s restrictions. The chapter lays unusually stringent purity restrictions on the high priest: he may not let his hair down, tear his clothes (the standard Israelite mourning gestures), or attend even his parents’ funeral (21:11–12). The provision sets the high priest one degree above ordinary priests, who could mourn close kin (21:1–4). The theological logic: the high priest in the role of mediator must remain ritually pristine, even at the cost of normal human grief. Caiaphas’s tearing his clothes at Jesus’ trial (Matt 26:65, Mark 14:63) is a deliberate violation of this verse — Mark’s wording ("the high priest tore his garments") is exact in its breach of Lev 21:10, and the gospel readers sensitive to Levitical detail would have recognized the procedural irregularity. Hebrews 4:14–15 takes the high priest’s strict separation as background for its argument about Christ as the high priest who is "able to sympathize with our weaknesses" — Christ as high priest specifically does not maintain Levitical separation from suffering. The verse is one of the OT’s most exact specifications of cultic role-discipline.

◇ Note. The Molech prohibition. Molech (Hebrew Molekh) is the deity of child-sacrifice the OT polemicizes against most consistently — cf. Lev 20:2–5, 1 Kgs 11:7 (Solomon’s Molech high place), 2 Kgs 23:10 (Josiah destroying the Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned), Jer 7:31, 19:5, 32:35. Most modern critical scholarship debates whether Molech was a separate deity, a title (the Hebrew root m-l-k means "king") for various ANE deities, or a specific sacrificial type (so M. Weinfeld read molekh as referring to a kind of votive offering rather than a god). Phoenician-Punic archaeological evidence (the tophet at Carthage and similar sites) confirms that infant sacrifice was a real ANE religious practice through the Iron Age. The Valley of Hinnom (Hebrew Gei Hinnom) became, by the time of the NT, the Hebrew root for "Gehenna" — Jesus’ word for the place of final judgment — precisely because of its association with child sacrifice. The verse is one of the OT’s clearest prohibitions of a real and recurring religious practice in the surrounding cultures, with long theological afterlife in both Jewish and Christian eschatological vocabulary.

◇ Note. The high priest’s marriage law. The chapter restricts the high priest to marrying only a virgin from his own people — explicitly excluding widows, divorced women, prostitutes, and "defiled" women that ordinary priests could marry (cf. 21:7, where ordinary priests are forbidden only the prostitute and the divorced woman). The provision intensifies the high priest’s ritual separation in personal life: even his marriage must perform the same purity-distinction his sanctuary work performs. The arrangement has long influenced Christian theological reflection on clerical celibacy and ministerial marriage — the medieval Latin church drew on the high priest’s separation to argue for clerical celibacy, while the Eastern church and most Protestant traditions have read the OT distinction as descriptive of an obsolete cultic role rather than prescriptive for Christian ministry. Heb 7:26–28 takes the high priest’s required perfection as background for its argument about Christ’s priestly office — the OT high priest’s rigorously specified separation becomes the foreshadowing the NT writer treats as fulfilled in the resurrected Christ "who has been made perfect forever."

וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן בְּקָרְבָתָ֥ם לִפְנֵי־יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּמֻֽתוּ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν, μετὰ τὸ τελευτῆσαι τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ἀαρὼν ἐν τῷ προσάγειν αὐτοὺς πῦρ ἀλλότριον ἔναντι Κυρίου, καὶ ἐτελεύτησαν.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:2.

And the LORD said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy [place] within the vail before the mercy seat, which [is] upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־אַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִיךָ֒ וְאַל־יָבֹ֤א בְכָל־עֵת֙ אֶל־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ מִבֵּ֖ית לַפָּרֹ֑כֶת אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַכַּפֹּ֜רֶת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַל־הָאָרֹן֙ וְלֹ֣א יָמ֔וּת כִּ֚י בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן אֵרָאֶ֖ה עַל־הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ εἶπε Κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν, λάλησον πρὸς Ἀαρὼν τὸν ἀδελφόν σου, καὶ μὴ εἰσπορευέσθω πᾶσαν ὥραν εἰς τὸ ἅγιον ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος εἰς πρόσωπον τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου, ὅ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται· ἐν γὰρ νεφέλῃ ὀφθήσομαι ἐπὶ τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:3.

Thus shall Aaron come into the holy [place:] with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Οὕτως εἰσελεύσεται Ἀαρὼν εἰς τὸ ἅγιον· ἐν μόσχῳ ἐκ βοῶν περὶ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ κριὸν εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:4.

He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these [are] holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and [so] put them on.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

כְּתֹֽנֶת־בַּ֨ד קֹ֜דֶשׁ יִלְבָּ֗שׁ וּמִֽכְנְסֵי־בַד֮ יִהְי֣וּ עַל־בְּשָׂרוֹ֒ וּבְאַבְנֵ֥ט בַּד֙ יַחְגֹּ֔ר וּבְמִצְנֶ֥פֶת בַּ֖ד יִצְנֹ֑ף בִּגְדֵי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֔ם וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֛יִם אֶת־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ וּלְבֵשָֽׁם׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ χιτῶνα λινοῦν ἡγιασμένον ἐνδύσεται, καὶ περισκελὲς λινοῦν ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ζώνῃ λινῇ ζώσεται, καὶ κίδαριν λινῆν περιθήσεται, ἱμάτια ἅγιά ἐστι· καὶ λούσεται ὕδατι πᾶν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνδύσεται αὐτά.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:5.

And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ παρὰ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ λήψεται δύο χιμάρους ἐξ αἰγῶν περὶ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ κριὸν ἕνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:6.

And Aaron shall offer his bullock of the sin offering, which [is] for himself, and make an atonement for himself, and for his house.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהִקְרִ֧יב אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־פַּ֥ר הַחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ προσάξει Ἀαρὼν τὸν μόσχον τὸν περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξιλάσεται περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:7.

And he shall take the two goats, and present them before the LORD [at] the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְלָקַ֖ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י הַשְּׂעִירִ֑ם וְהֶעֱמִ֤יד אֹתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:8.

And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְנָתַ֧ן אַהֲרֹ֛ן עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י הַשְּׂעִירִ֖ם גּוֹרָל֑וֹת גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וְגוֹרָ֥ל אֶחָ֖ד לַעֲזָאזֵֽל׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:9.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:10.

וְהַשָּׂעִ֗יר אֲשֶׁר֩ עָלָ֨ה עָלָ֤יו הַגּוֹרָל֙ לַעֲזָאזֵ֔ל יָֽעֳמַד־חַ֛י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְכַפֵּ֣ר עָלָ֑יו לְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֹת֛וֹ לַעֲזָאזֵ֖ל הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:11.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהִקְרִ֨יב אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־פַּ֤ר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּֽעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֣ד בֵּית֑וֹ וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת־פַּ֥ר הַֽחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:12.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:13.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:14.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:15.

¶ Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that [is] for the people, and bring his blood within the vail, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat:

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:16.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:17.

And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy [place], until he come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְכָל־אָדָ֞ם לֹא־יִהְיֶ֣ה ׀ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֗ד בְּבֹא֛וֹ לְכַפֵּ֥ר בַּקֹּ֖דֶשׁ עַד־צֵאת֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֤ר בַּעֲדוֹ֙ וּבְעַ֣ד בֵּית֔וֹ וּבְעַ֖ד כָּל־קְהַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:18.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְיָצָ֗א אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה וְכִפֶּ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וְלָקַ֞ח מִדַּ֤ם הַפָּר֙ וּמִדַּ֣ם הַשָּׂעִ֔יר וְנָתַ֛ן עַל־קַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ ἐξελεύσεται ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ὂν ἀπέναντι Κυρίου, καὶ ἐξιλάσεται ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ· καὶ λήψεται ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ μόσχου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ χιμάρου, καὶ ἐπιθήσει ἐπὶ τὰ κέρατα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου κύκλῳ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:19.

And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהִזָּ֨ה עָלָ֧יו מִן־הַדָּ֛ם בְּאֶצְבָּע֖וֹ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְטִהֲר֣וֹ וְקִדְּשׁ֔וֹ מִטֻּמְאֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 16:20.

Ἀπὸ προσώπου πολιοῦ ἐξαναστήσῃ, καὶ τιμήσεις πρόσωπον πρεσβυτέρου, καὶ φοβηθήσῃ τὸν Θεόν σου· ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 19:33.

¶ And if a stranger sojourn with thee in your land, ye shall not vex him.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְכִֽי־יָג֧וּר אִתְּךָ֛ גֵּ֖ר בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תוֹנ֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Ἐὰν δέ τις προσέλθῃ ὑμῖν προσήλυτος ἐν τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν, οὐ θλίψετε αὐτόν.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 19:34.

[But] the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I [am] the LORD your God.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Ὡς ὁ αὐτόχθων ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται ὁ προσήλυτος ὁ προσπορευόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἀγαπήσεις αὐτὸν ὡς σεαυτόν· ὅτι προσήλυτοι ἐγενήθητε ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ· ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 19:35.

¶ Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight, or in measure.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֖וֶל בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט בַּמִּדָּ֕ה בַּמִּשְׁקָ֖ל וּבַמְּשׂוּרָֽה׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Οὐ ποιήσετε ἄδικον ἐν κρίσει, ἐν μέτροις καὶ ἐν σταθμίοις καὶ ἐν ζυγοῖς.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 19:36.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I [am] the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

מֹ֧אזְנֵי צֶ֣דֶק אַבְנֵי־צֶ֗דֶק אֵ֥יפַת צֶ֛דֶק וְהִ֥ין צֶ֖דֶק יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Ζυγὰ δίκαια καὶ σταθμία δίκαια καὶ χοῦς δίκαιος ἔσται ἐν ὑμιν· ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν, ὁ ἐξαγαγὼν ὑμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 19:37.

Therefore shall ye observe all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: I [am] the LORD.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־כָּל ־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־ מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ φυλάξεσθε πάντα τὸν νόμον μου, καὶ πάντα τὰ προστάγματά μου, καὶ ποιήσετε αὐτά· ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:1.

And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν, λέγων, καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ λαλήσεις,

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:2.

Again, thou shalt say to the children of Israel, Whosoever [he be] of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn in Israel, that giveth [any] of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל תֹּאמַר֒ אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֩ מִבְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּמִן־הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן מִזַּרְע֛וֹ לַמֹּ֖לֶךְ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת עַ֥ם הָאָ֖רֶץ יִרְגְּמֻ֥הוּ בָאָֽבֶן׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

ἐάν τις ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν γεγενημένων προσηλύτων ἐν Ἰσραὴλ, ὃς ἂν δῷ τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτοῦ ἄρχοντι, θανάτῳ θανατούσθω· τὸ ἔθνος τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς λιθοβολήσουσιν αὐτὸν ἐν λίθοις.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:3.

And I will set my face against that man, and will cut him off from among his people; because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וַאֲנִ֞י אֶתֵּ֤ן אֶת־פָּנַי֙ בָּאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ מִקֶּ֣רֶב עַמּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י מִזַּרְעוֹ֙ נָתַ֣ן לַמֹּ֔לֶךְ לְמַ֗עַן טַמֵּא֙ אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וּלְחַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ ἐγὼ ἐπιστήσω τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐπὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκεῖνον, καὶ ἀπολῶ αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν ἄρχοντι, ἵνα μιάνῃ τὰ ἅγιά μου, καὶ βεβηλώσῃ τὸ ὄνομα τῶν ἡγιασμένων μοι.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:4.

And if the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not:

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְאִ֡ם הַעְלֵ֣ם יַעְלִימֽוּ֩ עַ֨ם הָאָ֜רֶץ אֶת־עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ מִן־הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא בְּתִתּ֥וֹ מִזַּרְע֖וֹ לַמֹּ֑לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הָמִ֥ית אֹתֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Ἐὰν δὲ ὑπερόψει ὑπερίδωσιν οἱ αὐτόχθονες τῆς γῆς τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου, ἐν τῷ δοῦναι αὐτὸν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτοῦ ἄρχοντι, τοῦ μὴ ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτόν·

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:5.

Then I will set my face against that man, and against his family, and will cut him off, and all that go a whoring after him, to commit whoredom with Molech, from among their people.

וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י אֲנִ֧י אֶת־פָּנַ֛י בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא וּבְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י אֹת֜וֹ וְאֵ֣ת ׀ כָּל־הַזֹּנִ֣ים אַחֲרָ֗יו לִזְנ֛וֹת אַחֲרֵ֥י הַמֹּ֖לֶךְ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:6.

¶ And the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits, and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהַנֶּ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּפְנֶ֤ה אֶל־הָֽאֹבֹת֙ וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים לִזְנ֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־פָּנַי֙ בַּנֶּ֣פֶשׁ הַהִ֔וא וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמּֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ ψυχὴ ἣ ἂν ἐπακολουθήσῃ ἐγγαστριμύθοις ἢ ἐπαοιδοῖς, ὥστε ἐκπορνεῦσαι ὀπίσω αὐτῶν, ἐπιστήσω τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἐκείνην, καὶ ἀπολῶ αὐτῆν ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτῆς.

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

Καὶ φυλάξεσθε τὰ προστάγματά μου, καὶ ποιήσετε αὐτά· ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζεν ὑμᾶς.

¶ For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood [shall be] upon him.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

כִּֽי־אִ֣ישׁ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְקַלֵּ֧ל אֶת־אָבִ֛יו וְאֶת־אִמּ֖וֹ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת אָבִ֧יו וְאִמּ֛וֹ קִלֵּ֖ל דָּמָ֥יו בּֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:10.

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:11.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

And if a man lie with his daughter in law, both of them shall surely be put to death: they have wrought confusion; their blood [shall be] upon them.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:13.

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:14.

And if a man take a wife and her mother, it [is] wickedness: they shall be burnt with fire, both he and they; that there be no wickedness among you.

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:15.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:16.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:17.

And if a man shall take his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it [is] a wicked thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of their people: he hath uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְאִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִקַּ֣ח אֶת־אֲחֹת֡וֹ בַּת־אָבִ֣יו א֣וֹ בַת־אִ֠מּוֹ וְרָאָ֨ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָ֜הּ וְהִֽיא־תִרְאֶ֤ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתוֹ֙ חֶ֣סֶד ה֔וּא וְנִ֨כְרְת֔וּ לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י עַמָּ֑ם עֶרְוַ֧ת אֲחֹת֛וֹ גִּלָּ֖ה עֲוֺנ֥וֹ יִשָּֽׂא׃

Greek (Septuagint / Brenton)

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:18.
